title: Training, inference, and where knowledge lives
outcome: Distinguish learned weights, request context, retrieved knowledge, and application memory.
cue: Weights learn patterns. Context carries this task. Your system owns current facts.
version: Provider-neutral principles · Ruby 3.3 / Rails 7.2 lab · legacy Ruby 2.7 adaptation notes
useCase: Distinguish learned weights, request context, retrieved knowledge, and application memory.
benefits: A clear decision and a way to check it.
drawbacks: “The model learned it in our chat” can hide application-managed history. A fresh call without that history may behave differently. Outdated indexes and caches can survive a correct source update.

trace.title: Training updates weights
trace.detail:
## Understand

Training updates model parameters from data. Inference uses a trained model to produce outputs.

A normal API conversation does not mean your application is updating the model’s weights during that conversation.

Pretraining learns broad statistical patterns. Instruction tuning and preference/reward-based post-training shape useful behavior.

These stages do not turn the model into your current production database. Provider data-use, logging, and retention policies are separate questions; “not training” does not mean “not stored.”

There are several places to put knowledge: weights, the current request, a retrieval index, a business database, and a stored conversation. They have different update and deletion paths.

Use current scoped queries for live counts. Use retrieval for relevant documents.

Consider fine-tuning for a measured behavior gap, not as the first way to keep yesterday’s inventory current.

trace.title: Follow one input
trace.detail:
Trace source update → ingestion → index publication → retrieval → answer cache. Separately trace conversation storage.

Ask how each place is corrected or deleted. Keep the model snapshot and prompt version in experiment records.
